mainTopic: An unborn baby's rights in inheritance, the בכור's double share, and gifts, plus a case of property left to future sons
overview: This amud finishes explaining why a one-day-old baby counts for inheritance but an עובר (unborn baby) does not. First, we assume an unborn baby dies before its mother, so it cannot inherit from her and pass it on to its father's side. Any movement afterward is just a reflex, like a lizard's cut-off tail. Then מר בריה דרב יוסף, quoting רבא, says a one-day-old baby reduces the בכור's double share but an unborn baby does not, because the פסוק says 'and they bore him'. In another version, taught in פומבדיתא, a בכור born after his father died gets no פי שנים, and the הלכה follows all the versions. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that a gift to a fetus does not take effect, except a father giving to his own son, while שמואל publicly disagrees. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן. Finally, a man leaves his property to his future sons and tells his older son to take a share like one of them, and two groups of אמוראים argue whether the older son gets that share. רבי אבהו and רבי ירמיה debate whose view is the הלכה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The unborn baby is assumed to die before its mother
steps.stepSummary: The explanation already underway finishes: an עובר does not inherit from its mother, because we assume it died first, and a dead son cannot inherit from his mother in the grave and pass it on to his brothers from his father's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the unborn baby dies first, and a son does not inherit from his mother while in the grave in order to pass it on to his brothers from his father's side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the reason why an unborn baby is left out of the rule that a baby inherits and passes on inheritance. It says the unborn baby is assumed to die before its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby died first, it was never alive to inherit from its mother. A son who dies before his mother cannot inherit from her 'in the grave' and pass her property to his half-brothers from his father. So the mother's property never reaches the father's family through this baby.

keyTerms.meaning: An unborn baby (still in the womb)

keyTerms.term: אֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר
keyTerms.meaning: A son does not inherit from his mother in the grave
To pass on an inheritance to others
Brothers from the father's side (not related to the mother)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean an unborn baby can never inherit at all. It only explains why an unborn baby does not inherit from its own mother when they both die, so the property cannot pass through it to the father's side.

phrases.english: Because it (the fetus) dies first,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר
phrases.english: and a son does not inherit from his mother in the grave
phrases.notes: 'In the grave' means after the son has already died, before his mother.

phrases.english: to pass it on to the brothers from the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהוּא מָיֵית בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation already in progress before this section began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unborn baby is assumed to die before its mother, so it does not inherit from her and pass it on to its paternal brothers.

steps.title: A real case where the baby moved after the mother died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that the unborn baby always dies first, citing a real event where the baby made three movements after the mother died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say it always dies first? But there was a real case, and the baby made three twitching movements!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea from step 1 that the unborn baby always dies first. It points to a real incident where the baby moved three times after the mother had died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby moved after the mother died, it seems the baby was still alive after her. Then it could have inherited from her and passed her property on, which breaks the reasoning of step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a challenge)
A real incident, an actual case

phrases.english: Is that to say that it dies first?!
But there was an incident,
and it twitched three twitches!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּהוּא מָיֵית בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual assumption of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the unborn baby always dies before its mother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real case showed the baby moving after the mother died, suggesting it was still alive after her.

steps.title: The movements were like a lizard's cut-off tail
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי answers that the baby's movements were only reflexes, like a lizard's tail that keeps jerking after it is cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: It is just like the tail of a lizard, which twitches.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי answers the challenge from step 2. He says the baby's movements did not prove it was alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lizard's tail keeps jerking after it is cut off, even though it is not alive. In the same way, the baby's three twitches were just leftover reflexes, so the assumption that it died first stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like… (introduces a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: An unborn baby is assumed to die before its mother, and any movement afterward is only a reflex, like a lizard's cut-off tail.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
It is just like the tail of a lizard, which twitches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַזְּנַב הַלְּטָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the evidence: the movements were reflexes, not signs of life.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The baby's movements after the mother's death show it was still alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The movements were only reflexes, like a lizard's tail, so the baby still counts as having died first.

steps.title: A different explanation: reducing the firstborn's share
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב יוסף, quoting רבא, explains the rule differently: a one-day-old baby reduces the firstborn's double portion, but an unborn baby does not, because the פסוק says 'and they bore him children'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר son of רב יוסף said in the name of רבא: The point is that a one-day-old reduces the firstborn's portion. And specifically a one-day-old, but not an unborn baby. What is the reason? The Torah says 'and they bore him children'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different explanation of why a one-day-old baby counts and an unborn baby does not. This time the topic is the firstborn's double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The firstborn gets a double share, figured by counting all the brothers. A one-day-old baby counts as a brother, so the firstborn's extra share is smaller. An unborn baby does not count, because the פסוק speaks of children already 'born' to the father.

keyTerms.meaning: The firstborn's extra (double) share of the inheritance
'And they bore him (children)' from the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new explanation, not a continuation of steps 1-3. Steps 1-3 were about inheriting from the mother; this step is about the firstborn's double share from the father.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical rule: when dividing the father's estate, only children already born count toward reducing the firstborn's double share.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
It comes to say that he reduces the firstborn's portion.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the one-day-old baby. Since he counts as a brother, the firstborn's extra share gets smaller.

phrases.aramaic: וְדַוְקָא בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד, אֲבָל עוּבָּר – לָא.
phrases.english: And specifically a one-day-old, but an unborn baby, no.
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said: 'And they bore him [children].'

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁמְּמַעֵט בְּחֵלֶק בְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the rule about a one-day-old baby versus an unborn baby, different from the one in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-day-old baby reduces the firstborn's double share, but an unborn baby does not, based on 'and they bore him'.

steps.title: Support from a son born after his father's death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up step 4 with another ruling of the same speaker: a son born after his father died does not reduce the firstborn's share, because 'and they bore him' does not apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As מר son of רב יוסף said in the name of רבא: A son born after his father's death does not reduce the firstborn's share. What is the reason? The Torah says 'and they bore him', and that is missing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule in step 4 matches another known ruling from the same teacher. A son born after his father died does not count against the firstborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and they bore him' mean the child must be born while the father is alive. A son still in the womb when his father died was not 'born to him' at that time. This is exactly why an unborn baby does not reduce the firstborn's share.

keyTerms.meaning: A son born after his father's death
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah / ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: Only a child born during the father's lifetime counts to reduce the firstborn's double share, because the Torah says 'and they bore him'.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: As Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava:
A son who was born after his father's death
does not reduce the firstborn's portion.
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said 'and they bore him,' and this is missing.
phrases.notes: He wasn't born while his father was alive, so he wasn't 'born to him'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4 by citing a parallel ruling from the same teacher based on the same פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That an unborn baby does not reduce the firstborn's share.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מר בריה דרב יוסף's ruling in the name of רבא that a son born after his father's death does not reduce the firstborn's share, based on 'and they bore him'.

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version: a posthumous firstborn gets no double portion
steps.stepSummary: In פומבדיתא, מר בריה דרב יוסף's teaching in the name of רבא was taught differently: a בכור born after his father's death does not take פי שנים, because the פסוק says יכיר, and the father is not there to acknowledge him.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught it the way we just learned. In פומבדיתא they taught it like this: מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא that a firstborn born after his father died does not get a double portion. Why? The Torah says 'he shall acknowledge' the firstborn, and here the father is not alive to acknowledge him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that a different yeshiva, פומבדיתא, remembered מר בריה דרב יוסף's teaching in a different way. In their version, the teaching is about the firstborn himself being born after the father died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4–5 were about whether a baby reduces the firstborn's share, based on 'and they bore him.' This version uses a different word, יכיר, 'he shall acknowledge.' A double portion depends on the father being able to recognize his firstborn, and a father who already died cannot do that.

keyTerms.meaning: A double portion, the firstborn's special share
He shall acknowledge (the father recognizing his firstborn)

phrases.english: In Sura, they taught it this way.
phrases.notes: 'This way' means the version you just learned in steps 4 and 5.

phrases.english: In Pumbedita, they taught it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Mar son of Rav Yosef said in the name of Rava:
A firstborn who was born after his father's death
does not take a double portion.
What is the reason?
The Merciful One said, 'He shall acknowledge,'
and here, he is not there to acknowledge him.
phrases.notes: The father has already died, so nobody can acknowledge this son as the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same speaker's teaching, as it was handed down in a different yeshiva.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור born after his father's death does not take פי שנים, because the father cannot fulfill יכיר.

steps.title: The הלכה follows every version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows all the versions of מר בריה דרב יוסף's teaching in the name of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows all of these versions of what מר בריה דרב יוסף said in the name of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this topic with a ruling. We do not have to choose between סורא and פומבדיתא, because we follow all the versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The versions do not contradict each other. Each one teaches a separate rule. A one-day-old baby reduces the firstborn's share, but an unborn baby or a son born after the father died does not. A firstborn born after his father died does not get a double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: Versions (different ways a teaching was passed down)

steps.whatToRemember: All three rules stand. A one-day-old baby reduces the בכור's share, but an unborn baby or a son born after the father's death does not. A בכור born after his father's death gets no פי שנים.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows all these versions

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: that Mar son of Rav Yosef said in the name of Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי לִישָּׁנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the practical law after both versions have been presented.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We follow every version of מר בריה דרב יוסף's teaching, since each one teaches a separate rule.

steps.title: A gift given to a fetus does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק quotes רבי יוחנן: someone who gives ownership of something to an עובר has not made a valid transfer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone gives something to an unborn baby, the baby does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן rules that an unborn baby cannot receive a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned two limits: an עובר does not inherit from its mother and pass it on to its father's side, and it does not reduce the בכור's share. Here the question is about a gift given on purpose. רבי יוחנן rules that a gift to a fetus does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: One who transfers ownership (gives something to someone)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who transfers ownership to a fetus, it does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from inheritance to gifts, while staying on the theme of an unborn child's rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift to an עובר does not take effect.

steps.title: But our משנה seems to say otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן raises a possible challenge against himself: our משנה seems to allow giving property to an unborn child.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: our משנה says otherwise!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings up an objection to his own rule before anyone else can. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה discusses a man who gives a gift to his unborn child, and it seems to treat that gift as valid. If that is so, a fetus can acquire, which contradicts the rule just stated.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introducing a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you will say: our mishna!
phrases.notes: He means the משנה in this perek about a man giving a gift to his own unborn child.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule using our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a gift to an עובר does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה appears to allow a gift to one's unborn child, which would mean a fetus can acquire.

steps.title: A father is especially close to his own son
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is a special case. A person feels very close to his own son, so a gift to one's own unborn child is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a person's mind is close to his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about a father giving to his own child, and that is a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays the same: a fetus cannot acquire. A father's strong closeness to his own son creates an exception. So the משנה does not prove that anyone can give a gift to any fetus.

keyTerms.term: דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קְרוֹבָה אֵצֶל בְּנוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person feels very close to his son

phrases.english: Since the mind of a person
is close to his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קְרוֹבָה אֵצֶל בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that any fetus can acquire a gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a father giving to his own unborn son is an exception, because of his closeness to his son. Otherwise a fetus does not acquire.

steps.title: שמואל publicly declares that a fetus does acquire
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב חנא בגדתאה to gather ten men so he can announce in front of them that a gift to an עובר does take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב חנא from Baghdad: Go bring me a group of ten men, and I will tell you in front of them: one who gives ownership to a fetus, it acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite opinion. שמואל holds that a fetus can acquire a gift, and he wants this said publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This disagrees directly with רבי יוחנן in step 8. Calling for ten men shows that שמואל wanted his ruling well known.

keyTerms.meaning: In their presence, in front of them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה:
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Chana of Baghdad:
Go out, bring me a group of ten,
and I will tell you in their presence:
One who transfers ownership to a fetus, it acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion that disagrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, a gift to an עובר does take effect.

steps.title: The הלכה: a fetus does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רבי יוחנן: a gift to an עובר does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: one who gives ownership to a fetus, it does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument between רבי יוחנן and שמואל, and rules like רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שמואל announced his view publicly, the final ruling is against him. A fetus cannot receive a gift, apart from the special case of a father giving to his own son.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן: a gift to an עובר does not take effect. The exception is a father giving to his own son.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not be thrown by שמואל's public announcement. The הלכה still goes against him.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
One who transfers ownership to a fetus, it does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא הַמְזַכֶּה לְעוּבָּר לֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between steps 8 and 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A gift to an עובר does not take effect, following רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A man leaves his property to future sons, and his older son asks for a share
steps.stepSummary: A man told his wife that his property goes to the sons he will have with her. His older son asked what he would get. The father told him to take a share like one of those sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his wife: 'My property is for the sons that I will have from you.' His older son came and said to him: 'What will become of that man (me)?' He said to him: 'Go acquire like one of the sons.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to test the rules about giving to children who do not exist yet. This sets up the comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons the father named were not even conceived yet. The older son is alive, and his father told him to take a share like theirs. This raises the question of what each of them actually received.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his wife:
"My property is for the sons that I will have from you."
His older son came,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״הַהוּא גַּבְרָא מַאי תֶּיהְוֵי עֲלֵיהּ?״
phrases.english: he said to him: "That man, what will become of him?"
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of saying 'me.'

phrases.english: He said to him: "Go acquire like one of the sons."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case about giving property to children who do not exist yet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father gave his property to future sons and told his living older son to take a share like one of them.

steps.title: The unborn sons certainly did not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא comments that the future sons surely did not acquire the gift, since they do not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those sons certainly did not acquire, because they do not exist yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its first comment on the story: the gift to the unborn sons does not work. This sets up the next question, which is what the older son gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a fetus cannot acquire, then sons who are not yet conceived surely cannot. That part is obvious. The open question is the older son's share, which the גמרא takes up next.

phrases.english: Those, certainly did not acquire,
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the future sons from the wife.

phrases.english: since they still do not exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ וַדַּאי לָא קָנוּ דְּאַכַּתִּי לֵיתַנְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling of step 12 to the story in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Sons who are not yet in existence cannot acquire a gift. What the older son gets is taken up in step 15.

steps.title: Does the older son get his promised share?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the older son receives the extra share his father promised him alongside the other sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about this older son? Does the young man get a share where there are sons, or does he not get a share where there are sons?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the older son from the story. The future sons did not acquire their gift, so what happens to the older son's promised share?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father linked the older son's share to the shares of the future sons: 'take a share like one of them.' Since we just said the gift to the future sons did not work, the question is whether the older son's extra share still holds. This question sets up the argument that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A young man, the older son in our story
Where there are sons, alongside the other sons

phrases.english: This [son]—
phrases.notes: This is the older son from the story, the one his father told to take a share like one of the future sons.

phrases.english: does the young man have a share where there are sons,
or does the young man not have a share
where there are sons?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אִית חוּלָק לְטַלְיָא בִּמְקוֹם בְּנַיָּא אוֹ לֵית לֵיהּ חוּלָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 14: the future sons did not acquire, so now we ask about the older son.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the older son gets the extra share promised to him alongside the other sons.

steps.title: First group says he does get a share
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין, רבי מיישא and רבי ירמיה say the young man does get a share where there are sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין, רבי מיישא and רבי ירמיה say: the young man does get a share where there are sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer. Three אמוראים say the older son does get his promised share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, the older son keeps his extra share even though the gift to the future sons did not work. The next step brings the opposite view.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַבִּי מְיָישָׁא וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה דְּאָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin and Rabbi Meyasha and Rabbi Yirmeya, who say:
The young man has a share where there are sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַבִּי מְיָישָׁא וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the older son gets the share.

steps.title: Second group says he does not get a share
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי יצחק נפחא say the young man does not get a share where there are sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי יצחק נפחא say: the young man does not get a share where there are sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite opinion. Three other אמוראים say the older son does not get his promised share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have an even split, three against three. This sets up the next question: whose view is the הלכה?

keyTerms.meaning: There is not, he does not have
The smith, a nickname of רבי יצחק

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi
and Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa, who say:
The young man has no share where there are sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפִּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes the view of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The older son does not get the share.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, the older son does not get the share.

steps.title: Whose view is the הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks רבי ירמיה whether the הלכה follows his group or the other group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said to רבי ירמיה: Is the הלכה like us, or is the הלכה like you?
steps.whatsHappening: A member of each side now talks directly to the other. רבי אבהו asks which view is the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו is from the 'no share' group and רבי ירמיה is from the 'yes share' group. The question moves from what each side holds to which side wins.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said to Rabbi Yirmeya:
Is the halakha like us,
or is the halakha like you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתַן אוֹ הִלְכְתָא כְּוָתַיְיכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both views are stated, asks which one is the הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which group's view is the final הלכה.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: we are older, so we win
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the הלכה is obviously like his group, because they are older and the other group is young.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is obvious that the הלכה is like us, because we are older than you. The הלכה is not like you, because you are youngsters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers that his side wins. His reason is that his group is older than רבי אבהו's group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה uses seniority as the deciding factor: the older scholars should be followed. He does not give any reason based on the case itself. The next step challenges this.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is obvious that the halakha is like us—
since we are older than you,
and the halakha is not like you—
since you are youngsters.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא דְּהִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתַן דְּקַשִּׁישְׁנָא מִינַּיְיכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבהו's question from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows the older group, which is רבי ירמיה's group.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: it depends on the reason, not age
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rejects the age argument and says the matter depends on the reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does the matter depend on age? The matter depends on the reason!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו pushes back. Being older does not decide the הלכה; the strength of the reasoning does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rejects the basis of רבי ירמיה's answer, not his view itself. Once age is set aside, the question becomes: what is the reasoning? That sets up the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבי אבהו is answering back.

phrases.english: Does the matter depend on age?!
The matter depends on the reason!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי בְּקַשִּׁישׁוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the age-based answer of step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects age as the way to decide the הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Seniority is not a reason; the הלכה depends on the logic of the ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It states a basic idea: a ruling is decided by its reasoning, not by the age of the scholars who hold it.

steps.title: What is your reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אבהו to give his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי אבהו said the reason is what counts, רבי ירמיה asks him what his reason is. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion now turns from who is older to the actual logic behind the 'no share' view.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה is asking רבי אבהו for the reason behind his group's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 20 by asking for the reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind the view that the older son gets no share.

steps.title: Go ask רבי אבין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו tells רבי ירמיה to go to רבי אבין, because he already explained the reason to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Go to רבי אבין, because I explained it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו does not give the reason here directly. He sends רבי ירמיה to רבי אבין, to whom he had explained it. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין was listed in step 16 on רבי ירמיה's own side. Yet רבי אבהו says he explained his reasoning to רבי אבין. What happened with רבי אבין is told in the continuation.

phrases.english: Go to Rabbi Avin—
phrases.notes: רבי אבין was named in step 16 as one of the 'yes share' group.

phrases.english: for I explained it to him,

steps.triggerLanguage: זִיל לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין דְּאַסְבַּרְתַּהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 by sending רבי ירמיה to רבי אבין.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבין already heard the reason from רבי אבהו, so ask him.
